title: Per-route cost-aware admission and priority throttler for realtime console metrics
creator: Asha K. Patel
description:
Background: The console metrics ingest pipeline has intermittent overload events when bursty customers and expensive enrichment correlate (large JSONs + per-event model lookups). Current coarse per-tenant limits either let expensive routes starve safe routes or force broad throttles that hurt critical dashboards. Goal: implement a lightweight per-route, cost-aware admission controller and prioritization layer in the ingest fronting tier (ingest-proxy) that enforces soft budgets based on observed token/event cost estimates and upstream SLOs.

Objectives:
- Track per-route and per-tenant cost budgets (tokens/event) over sliding windows and admit/reject with priority-aware rules.
- Support dynamic priority mappings: e.g., critical dashboards (route: /events/heartbeat) = high priority, debug/logging = low priority. Priorities influence admission and graceful degradation order.
- Implement soft-failover: on overload, route low-priority events to cheaper storage (ingest-s3) or sampling instead of immediate drop.
- Provide observability: per-route accept/reject rate, queue depth, estimated token cost, and budget burn-down.
- Feature-flagged rollout with canary and kill switch accessible in Console.

Design decisions and trade-offs:
- Location: implement throttler in ingest-proxy (Go) to minimize cross-service coordination and allow early admission control. This favors simplicity vs. central controller complexity.
- Budgeting model: use a leaky-bucket reservoir per (tenant, route) weighted by recent median token cost. We approximate token cost from event size & known enrichment flags to keep runtime overhead low.
- Priority handling: implement three priority bands (P0/P1/P2). P0 bypasses soft limits up to a small emergency queue to protect control-plane events. P2 is candidate for sampling or cheap-store fallback. This avoids complete denial for low-value telemetry.
- Metrics collection overhead: we batch budget updates asynchronously and use probabilistic counters for high-cardinality routes to avoid metric explosion.

Acceptance criteria (must pass to close):
- Unit + integration tests covering admission decisions for different priority and cost scenarios.
- Load test: With synthetic mix (10% P0, 30% P1, 60% P2) at 2x peak ingest, overall console latency p95 <= existing SLO + 50ms and dropped-event rate for P0 < 0.1%, for P1 < 1%.
- Canary rollout runs for 72 hours with metrics showing stable budget behavior and no alert storms.
- Dashboards created: grafana panel + alert if rejected_rate > 2% for P1 or queue_depth > 3000 for any tenant.
- Docs: Confluence design doc and runbook linked.

Implementation plan:
1) Prototype: implement a simple per-route reservoir + admission decision (in Go) behind a feature flag. Measure CPU/heap overhead for 5K active routes.
2) Integrate soft-failover paths (writes to cheap-store or sample pipeline) and ensure downstream consumers can tag degraded events.
3) Add observability and admin endpoints (current budget, last decision, suggested override).
4) Load-test in staging with synthetic traffic and chaos scenarios (shard failures, slow downstream).
5) Canary: route 5% of production tenants for 24h, expand to 25% then 100% with kill switch.

Rollout & operational notes:
- Feature flag initially default-off. Canary controlled via console toggle and rollout policy.
- Emergency kill switch implemented as two levels: global and tenant-scoped.
- SLA obligation: on detection of misconfiguration causing excessive P0 rejects, auto-disable and open incident.

Observability & dashboards:
- Grafana panels: per-route burn-rate, accept/reject ratio by priority, estimated token-cost histogram, per-tenant queue-depth.
- Alerts: high reject rate per-priority, sustained budget exhaustion > 60s, surge CPU on ingest-proxy.

Links and artifacts:
- Confluence design: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/ENG/Per-Route+Cost-Aware+Throttler
- GitHub prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ingest/pull/4321
- Load test results (staging): https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/ingest/loadtests/eng-998001
- Runbook stub: https://confluence.redwood.ai/pages/viewpage.action?pageId=12345678

Notes on future work:
- Replace heuristic token-cost with model-based estimator from Optimize team (medium-term).
- Evaluate central cost controller for global rebalancing across regions.

This ticket focuses on the initial per-proxy implementation, observability, and safe rollout.
